task: Core #1186 F6-U03k: source-pinned ordered Office predecessor replay on disposable Docker PG17, fail closed on next dependency

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Critical real Docker-only negative SQL proof. Extra original source files are candidate diagnostic inputs, NOT migration approval. No live server, SQL authoring, or security policy override.

acceptanceCriteria: Original frozen 59 filenames, bytes and source digest verified by validateReviewedBaseline; 18 main Git blobs verified by F6-U03j inspectOfficeGap without rewriting original SQL.

Single BEGIN and COMMIT envelopes entire original 59 SQL plus exactly 18 original timestamped Office candidate SQL files BEFORE original 0055, plus authentic target preflight/auth-bootstrap/neutral seed/postflight.
Docker peer IP, name, postgres role and real PG17 verification and rejection of inherited PGHOST, PGHOSTADDR, PGDATABASE, DATABASE_URL and Supabase selectors enforced before any SQL.
Failure to execute any statement is recorded as LOCAL_SOURCE_BLOCKED with actual psql SQLSTATE/error line and no 59+18 COMMIT claim; verify no application schema persisted.
Only genuine postflight and committed schema can yield LOCAL_SOURCE_REPLAY_COMMITTED; even then an independent pre-COMMIT fault must prove rollback and release stays blocked.
Original 59-file F6-U03b hosted compiler abort-before-DROP and F6-U03f full strict guard unchanged, no hosted writes or managed provider acceptance.
Separate exact-head source workflow and normal CI/Truth/Lifecycle gates provide reproducible evidence.
invariants: Never edit or copy original 59 or 18 source SQL; treat main timestamped candidate files as diagnostic only, not release authority.
Source concatenator has no database connection, network or filesystem write outside artifacts/f6-u03k source bundle output.
Every DB connection in workflow uses -h 127.0.0.1 Docker published ports, pinned local database names only, no inherited external libpq selector.
Preserve original target-preflight/target-postflight/neutral seed in transaction and full source content, never weaken preflight or install synthetic office tables.
psql ON_ERROR_STOP=1 and actual nonzero exit required for SQL failure; classify blocked, never success as readiness.
Full hosted F6-U03b execution abort remains before schema DROP and no transaction guard production code changes.
forbiddenStates: Any CI job connects to Supabase waterk-platform, waterk-staging, or Fresh Install.
Fake green source replay by swallowing psql error without recording blocked SQLSTATE/transaction aftermath.
Insertion of synthetic Office tables or material provider implementations not present in original sources.
Candidate timestamped SQL treated as approved release package or applied to active project.
Full provider/TLS/JWT/tenant authorization reported proven from local Docker.
Original F6-U03f security gate or 59-file source bytes rewritten for test success.

failureModes: The 18-source prelude depends on an omitted older migration with an undefined private function or table, leading to a genuine PostgreSQL error before 0055.
An older Office source grants excessive role permissions or overrides later Pro-only policy; local SQL may run but is not production-appropriate.
Read-only aftermath misses public/private functions created outside the transaction by accidental autocommit.
psql exits zero despite SQL errors if ON_ERROR_STOP is dropped or a shell status is lost.
A duplicate 0026 original file is omitted in source translation and produces misleading count 59.
Injected failure is placed after COMMIT or uses the same committed database, not a distinct fixture.
edgeCases: A source SQL text contains comments with BEGIN/COMMIT but no actual nested transaction; envelope identification uses explicit compiler markers.
An extra SQL source introduces function bodies containing the text 'COMMIT;' but no top-level transaction end.
A Source file contains a line with psql meta commands or COPY and changes execution semantics; classify and preserve instead of suppress.
Different original SQL migration files define the same function with CREATE OR REPLACE; local replay is diagnostic only, not release ownership.
A real 59+18 local run fails after preflight but prior to 0055, leaving no committed application objects.
Original target-postflight assumes only 59 migration RLS policy counts and may fail after additional candidate sources: report exact result rather than change it.

specialistReviews.finding: Older timestamped Office SQL may carry stale grants or blanket-Pro policies and cannot be approved for runtime from a successful local replay.
specialistReviews.resolution: Only Docker diagnostic; manifest release=false and explicit supersession/role/tenant gate separate.

specialistReviews.finding: An apparently successful append may hide incomplete source order and multi-transaction commits.
specialistReviews.resolution: One BEGIN/COMMIT with sources before 0055 and mandatory postflight/rollback or exact failure aftermath.

specialistReviews.finding: A source file can be changed between DAG scan and execution.
specialistReviews.resolution: Pin 18 main Git blob bytes and 59 approved source hashes in every emitted manifest; run Git SHA checks before CLI output.

specialistReviews.finding: Passing CI for blocked diagnostic can be incorrectly promoted to hosted deployment.
specialistReviews.resolution: Separate workflow gate name, machine result RELEASE_NOT_AUTHORIZED, unchanged hosted guard and #1228 open.

challenge.scenario: After original 0054, a candidate 20260908030000 adds required mailbox tables but another prior function dependency is missing, so the source replay fails inside the one transaction.
challenge.finding: Treating a different SQL error as permission to skip the failing candidate would mask a release source gap and fabricate full 59+18 installation readiness.
challenge.resolution: Capture actual nonzero psql error, source filename and line with transaction rollback, mark BLOCKED, and keep #1228 open until separately versioned source DAG correction.

challenge.scenario: The candidate old Office inbound SQL contains a RLS policy that grants a legacy role access inconsistent with current Alap/Pro contract.
challenge.finding: Even if all 77 source SQL files run successfully on a temporary database, that does not prove safe modern tenant authorization or final SQL package precedence.
challenge.resolution: Do not mark release APPROVED; require independent policy and grants diff, supersession scan and authenticated Alap/Pro RLS proof before approval.

challenge.scenario: A CI command accidentally points 127.0.0.1 to a non-Docker PostgreSQL instance or inherits PGHOSTADDR, DATABASE_URL or SUPABASE_DB_URL.
challenge.finding: A destructive historical baseline execution could target an unauthorized hosted database if peer identity is not proved before connecting.
challenge.resolution: Use two verified Docker PG17 container identities, fixed local DB/ports, exact server peer IP, role, major version and reject all inherited libpq selectors.

challenge.scenario: One of the 18 candidate source SQL blobs or original 59 reviewed migrations is modified while filenames and counts stay unchanged.
challenge.finding: A 77-filename count is insufficient provenance and could silently conceal an edited security policy or SQL statement.
challenge.resolution: Require both existing reviewed baseline Git-blob verifier and main authoritative blob SHA check of each 18 original Office file before emitting SQL.

challenge.scenario: The temporary SQL uses two BEGIN/COMMIT envelopes or places a candidate after original 0055 rather than immediately before it.
challenge.finding: A second transaction could commit half the schema, while the immutable 0055 still reaches a missing relation and fails.
challenge.resolution: Compose one protected transaction using existing F6-U03i SQL and insert all verified predecessor source chunks before the original 0055 marker, checking exact position and one outer envelope.

challenge.scenario: A psql execution fails at 0055 but shell script ignores status and prints SUCCESS based only on raw output containing earlier preflight marker.
challenge.finding: The SQL replay is falsely certified even though no valid COMMIT or postflight completed, potentially authorizing live schema reset.
challenge.resolution: Use ON_ERROR_STOP=1, capture real exit status separately, inspect psql error and post-run actual DB object counts, and emit explicit BLOCKED result with no release authorization.

challenge.scenario: All original SQL and postflight pass in local fixture yet the failure injection runs after COMMIT or on the same database, proving no rollback.
challenge.finding: Database atomicity cannot be claimed from a failure raised after commit or a count query against an already persisted schema.
challenge.resolution: Use separate fresh Docker PG17 database and inject exception before only COMMIT; require nonzero exit and zero app-owned relations/functions/policies before accepting local rollback proof.

challenge.scenario: The local 77-source replay succeeds using synthetic Auth/Storage provider roles, and the completion message claims full signed-in Alap/Pro RLS and hosted managed restore are done.
challenge.finding: Local Postgres role mocks have no provider event semantics, TLS host proof, JWT boundary enforcement or customer Data API and cannot prove release readiness.
challenge.resolution: Hardcode releaseAuthorized=false, hostedTouched=false, providerProven=false, authenticatedTenantRlsProven=false in every result and require later independent acceptance.
